## Highlights

- **Config trust closes the remaining bypasses.** A committed `.sekretbarilo.toml` is trusted only when the bytes the hook parses equal its blob at `HEAD`, read once from a regular file. `git update-index --assume-unchanged`, `--skip-worktree` and replace refs no longer hide a permissive edit. A working directory reached through a symlink into another repository no longer picks up config layers that the repository holding the link does not vouch for.
- **`doctor` and the hooks agree.** `doctor` judges config layers with the same function the agent hooks use. It also reports a local pre-commit hook that a global `core.hooksPath` bypasses.
- **Weekly fuzzing is green again.** Two fuzz oracles had drifted from the scanner's contracts, and a malformed hunk header could overflow the diff parser. All eight fuzz targets now run clean.
- **Release notes are written by hand.** The GitHub release body comes from `.github/release-notes/v<version>.md` instead of a changelog generated from squash commits. The 0.9.0, 0.9.1 and 0.10.0 releases were rewritten the same way.

## Upgrade notes

- A relative or empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is ignored, and the user config is read from `~/.config`, as the XDG base directory specification says. An empty `HOME` counts as unset.
- If a committed config layer's checkout differs from its blob only through `core.autocrlf`, `eol` or a smudge filter, the agent hooks now treat it as modified and drop it. `doctor` reports it.
- `install pre-commit` without `--global`, and the pre-commit part of `install all`, exits 2 when `core.hooksPath` comes from the global or system git config, because git never runs a hook in `.git/hooks` then. Use `install pre-commit --global`, or unset `core.hooksPath`.
- A bare `token` key must have its separator on the same line, so a slice index such as `window[\n token\n :\n "..."\n]` is no longer reported. Quoted keys and the YAML form `token:\n  "..."` are still read.

Upgrade: `brew upgrade vshuraeff/tap/sekretbarilo`, then `sekretbarilo doctor`.

## Changes

### Config trust for the agent hooks
- How a committed layer is read:
  - `lstat` must show a regular file, and the opened file must have the same device and inode.
  - Its bytes must equal `git --no-replace-objects cat-file blob HEAD:<path>`.
  - Exactly those bytes are parsed.
- Through a symlink from one repository into another, the target's in-workspace layers are dropped with a warning. A layer inside the repository holding the link must be committed and unmodified in that repository. A symlink within the same repository keeps its layers.
- Discovery ignores a relative or empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and an empty `HOME`.

### Doctor and install
- `doctor` reports symlinked layers alongside untracked and modified ones. It no longer warns about an uncommitted user layer in a dotfiles repository at `HOME`.
- `doctor` prints an info line when a global or system `core.hooksPath` bypasses the local pre-commit hook. A repository-local `core.hooksPath` still counts as the repository's own hook directory.

### Detection
- New contextual rule `infisical-client-id`. Together with the existing named-key rules, `redact-claude` now masks `INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID`, `VAST_AI_API_KEY`, `ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY` and `PUSHOVER_APP_TOKEN` values in `pgrep -fl` and `ps` output. That makes 114 built-in rules, 110 on by default.
- Rules take three new optional fields:
  - `payload_group` selects the payload without its provider prefix.
  - `min_payload_entropy` sets an entropy floor for that payload.
  - `reject_hex_payload` rejects an all-hex payload.
- The OpenAI project-key and Facebook token checks now come from these fields instead of code. Findings are byte-identical on the reference corpus.
- Named capture groups are resolved once per rule at compile time instead of on every match.
- The diff parser saturates line numbers on a hunk header near `usize::MAX` instead of panicking. It keeps every added line.

### Docs, CI and release
- The getting-started, installation, configuration and agent-hooks pages each belong to one Diataxis quadrant. Explanations moved to "How the agent hooks work", and the old anchors still resolve.
- `release.yml` publishes `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`. It fails before any build when that file is missing, empty or starts with a version heading. git-cliff and `cliff.toml` are removed.
- The `literals` and `predicates` fuzz oracles match the scanner contracts: Go struct-tag items nest inside the tag, and hex lengths run from 32 to 128. Every crash input is kept in the corpus.
- New binary-level tests cover the trust bypasses above, `check-file` with symlinked and user layers, and argv redaction.
